photos.caption: Figure 5.1 · Instruments follow a changing geometry. Antennas at NASA's Goldstone Deep Space Network complex, photographed in February 2020. Tracking a spacecraft involves changing positions and directions. This photograph supplies an instrument setting, not measurements for the simplified rate models used in this unit. Credit: Courtesy NASA/JPL-Caltech, PIA23214. Image source · Reuse terms . Unmodified source rendition; display scaling only. No endorsement implied.

Figure 5.2 · A path does not specify a rate. Curiosity's navigation-camera panorama from 8 June 2023 records tracks left while backing up and repositioning near an obstacle. Tracks reveal a route, but the image alone does not tell us the elapsed time between chosen positions. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech, PIA26015. Source and description · Reuse terms . Unmodified panorama, scaled for display.

Figure 5.9 · A surface and incoming light. ISS solar arrays, photographed by the Expedition 40 crew in August 2014. Revisited from Unit 2: the panels provide a setting for considering a projected area and how that area changes with angle. Perspective does not supply a measured angle or a power curve. Credit: NASA / Expedition 40 crew, ISS040-E-087239. Source · NASA reuse terms . Existing recompressed image; no geometric alterations.

Figure 5.11 · An instrument suggests more than one changing factor. The Goldstone photograph from the unit opening returns here as a setting for a deliberately simplified collection model. No receiving area, illumination or measured power is extracted from the image. Credit: Courtesy NASA/JPL-Caltech, PIA23214. Source · Reuse terms . Unmodified rendition.

Figure 5.15 · Which variable is changing? NIST thermometer calibration, revisited from Unit 4. A temperature, an instrument reading and a displayed output can be related by different functions. Their derivatives refer to different pairs of variables; converting between rates requires the corresponding local conversion factor. Credit: NIST, 11PML009, 2011. Source · Reuse terms . Unmodified; US-government work, with NIST's foreign-copyright qualification retained.

Figure 5.18 · A position is not a velocity or an acceleration. An Astrobee robot aboard the International Space Station in May 2023. The scene, revisited from Unit 1, is a reminder of three different descriptions of motion. One photograph cannot determine a velocity or acceleration; our cubic model is not a reconstruction of this robot's trajectory. Credit: NASA, ISS069-E-010815. Source · NASA reuse terms . Unaltered image, scaled for display.

Figure 5.20 · Verification is a mathematical task. Katherine Johnson at NASA Langley in 1966. NASA's account describes her verification of electronic-computer calculations for John Glenn's orbital flight. Our small investigation is an exercise in checking a model calculation, not a reconstruction of that orbital work. Credit: NASA, 1966-L-06717. Source and historical context · NASA reuse terms . Existing teaching image, scaled for display.

original_diagrams: Thirteen original SVG figures, CC BY-NC-SA4.0. Function/derivative curves, secants/tangents, product increment, chain stages, circle branches and second-rate graphs checked against formulas. Captions state model and domain/scale limitations; colours accompanied by labels/dashes.
interactive_decision: ActiveCalculus1.1 secant/velocity exploration inspected. Static comparisons keep both signs, branches and rates visible together; two-hour learner-controlled Python investigation tests an actual error and domain/rounding limits. No additional animation selected. This is an explicit selection after planning, not an exemption from media richness.
video_decision: Video opportunity considered for tangent motion; no video recommended because no inspected candidate added a necessary perspective beyond original diagrams and the investigation. No claim that a video was watched.
review: Source pages and terms inspected; actual assets viewed. New Goldstone and existing NASA/NIST images checked against specific source descriptions. All7 teaching fragments pass structural media audit. Human visual inspection complements the structural check.
